          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 6
        
      
                          
                      Oct 8, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Looking for an edge with under-the-radar picks in Fantasy Premier League? Well, The 10% Club is back to help following the international break.
The extended international break is finally over, and although you might have a few new injury concerns, that also means Fantasy Premier League returns this weekend.
Indeed, managers opening up their teams may be greeted with red and yellow hazard signs galore after numerous players withdrew either before or during the international window.
However, we have some options in The 10% Club to cover those potential gaps. Using Opta data, here are our five under-the-radar picks for Gameweek 6.
A hard-fought goalless draw away to Leeds United may have slightly eased the pressure on Pierre Sage, and he will be desperate for Crystal Palace to improve further after the break.
Having kept their first clean sheet of the season at Elland Road, Tyrick Mitchell is an interesting pick for when goal-shy Nottingham Forest visit south east London.
Forest, managed by former Palace boss Oliver Glasner, have scored just four times this season, with only two sides – Tottenham (2) and Coventry City (1) – finding the net on fewer occasions.
No Palace player can better Mitchell’s 24 points this season either, partly due to the attacking threat he can pose.

He's never been a particularly frequent source of goals, though his two in the league this term is the most of any defender. That could easily have turned to three goals as well, if not for a VAR review seeing Mitchell’s sumptuous strike against Leeds ruled out for an Anan Khalaili offside in the build-up.

It's worth saying, however, that Mitchell’s two biggest points hauls – 15 against Fulham and 7 against Leeds – came away from home. Sage will have designs on Palace turning around their home form this weekend, though.

Mitchell’s affordable price point could also help managers find room for the likes of James Tarkowski, Josko Gvardiol or Riccardo Calafiori, with the option to leave Mitchell on the bench when Palace visit free-scoring Brighton on GW7.

Many managers this season are opting to target whoever is playing Coventry. Their 1-0 away win last time out over Forest may have perturbed some, but those sticking to that plan will note they host Newcastle United.
Lewis Hall and Yoane Wissa are both off the cards due to their ownership proportions, but Harvey Barnes has scored the second-most points (28 – behind only Hall’s 31) for Newcastle.
Barnes claimed nine points against Hull City before the break after assisting twice in one Premier League match for the first time since May 2022 (for Leicester City against Norwich City).

He has been Newcastle’s main creative threat this term, leading the way with six chances created and all of them were from open play. Hall is second on the list with five, but that is aided by two from set-pieces.

More goals may not be far away for Barnes. Only Joe Willock (10) and Wissa (9) have had more than his eight shots for Newcastle, though Barnes has just one goal – a stunning strike against Bournemouth on GW3 – to show for his efforts.
Barnes then faces Aston Villa (H), Palace (A), Everton (H) and Fulham (A), and that fairly favourable run may see FPL players splashing out on Newcastle assets.
With Ipswich Town next hosting Fulham, Gary O’Neil will see it as a great chance to pick up three points against Álvaro Arbeloa’s winless side.
Although Julio Enciso is yet to score this season, we believe he could make the difference for Ipswich on GW6. The Paraguayan did also manage two assists from his opening two games.

No Ipswich player has attempted more shots than Enciso’s 17, while his four shots on target is only matched by Emersonn. Abdul Fatawu (1.1) has marginally bettered his 0.9 expected assists (xA), but the winger is suspended after his red card at Everton.
